content.content:
Web search results for query: "Supabase docs Row Level Security guide"

Links: [{"title":"Row Level Security","url":"https://supabase.com/docs/guides/database/postgres/row-level-security"},{"title":"Securing your API","url":"https://supabase.com/docs/guides/api/securing-your-api"},{"title":"Securing your data","url":"https://supabase.com/docs/guides/database/secure-data"},{"title":"RAG with Permissions","url":"https://supabase.com/docs/guides/ai/rag-with-permissions"},{"title":"Database","url":"https://supabase.com/docs/guides/database/overview"},{"title":"Tables and data","url":"https://supabase.com/docs/guides/database/tables"},{"title":"Introducing: Postgres Best Practices","url":"https://supabase.com/blog/postgres-best-practices-for-ai-agents"},{"title":"API keys","url":"https://supabase.com/docs/guides/getting-started/api-keys"},{"title":"Realtime Authorization","url":"https://supabase.com/docs/guides/realtime/authorization"},{"title":"Production Checklist","url":"https://supabase.com/docs/guides/deployment/going-into-prod"}]

The top result is Supabase's main Row Level Security guide, and it's split into three parts: an explanation of how grants and policies combine, a step-by-step procedure for securing each table, and a reference for helper functions and policy patterns. ([supabase.com/docs/guides/database/postgres/row-level-security](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/database/postgres/row-level-security))

Key points from that guide:
- **Grants and policies work as separate checks.** Grants control whether a role can run an operation on a table at all, and policies control which rows that operation can touch. ([Row Level Security guide](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/database/postgres/row-level-security))
- **Default grants can be a risk.** Newer projects may still grant broad access to the anon and authenticated roles automatically, so the guide advises revoking those grants. ([Row Level Security guide](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/database/postgres/row-level-security))
- **Write one policy per operation.** The guide recommends separate policies for select, insert, update, and delete, and it explains how `using` and `with check` differ. ([Row Level Security guide](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/database/postgres/row-level-security))
- **Testing is part of the procedure.** It recommends a SQL test file and running `supabase test db` before trusting the policies. ([Row Level Security guide](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/database/postgres/row-level-security))
- **Views need extra care.** Views can bypass RLS by default, and on Postgres 15+ the guide suggests setting `security_invoker = true`. ([Row Level Security guide](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/database/postgres/row-level-security))

Related pages in the results include the Securing your API guide, the API keys page (which explains that secret keys bypass RLS), the Tables and data page, and the Production Checklist.
